correctness.rationale: The algebraic statements derived from the EXPLICIT surrogate definition m_B=min{m:Σ_i w_i* w_i=I_B} are true: trace energy averaging gives sqrt(τ(1)/m_B)≤||iota||≤sqrt τ(1), and on M_{r,s}, ||iota||²=c min(r,s), m_B=ceil(s/r). However the result repeatedly identifies this number as the least length of a finite Parseval RIGHT MODULE FRAME and claims it obstructs standard right module-frame rank. In the established Hilbert C*-module definition (Frank–Larson arXiv:math/0010189, Def.2 and reconstruction formula Thm.4.1), a finite right Parseval frame must satisfy x=Σ_i w_i〈w_i,x〉_B for EVERY x, equivalently Σ_i w_i w_i*=I_r on Z=M_{r,s}, not Σ_i w_i* w_i=I_s. Concrete decisive counterexample r=1,s=2: Z=M_{1,2}, w=(1,0). Then for every row X, w(w*X)=X, so {w} is a one-vector right Parseval frame; the claim says minimum ceil(2/1)=2. For trace τ=Tr_2, ||iota||=1, so the asserted purported right-frame lower bound would say sqrt(2/1)≤1, false. The paper’s private definition instead measures a B-normalizing family/dual left frame; it does not justify the stated interpretation as right-frame rank. No complete repaired claim/files were supplied. Thus the final claimed right-frame theorem is false although its differently named B-normalizing inequalities survive algebraically.
